title: Supreme Court: Chiles v. Salazar
summary: Colorado’s law banning conversion therapy, as applied to petitioner’s talk therapy, regulates speech based on viewpoint, and the lower courts erred by failing to apply sufficiently rigorous First Amendment scrutiny. (No. 24-539, opinion by Justice Gorsuch; 607 U.S. 627).

title: Supreme Court: Rico v. United States
summary: The Sentencing Reform Act of 1984 does not authorize a rule automatically extending a defendant’s term of supervised release when the defendant fails to report to a probation officer. (No. 24-1056, opinion by Justice Gorsuch; 607 U.S. 609).

title: Supreme Court: Cox Communications, Inc. v. Sony Music Entertainment
summary: Internet service provider Cox Communications neither induced its users’ infringement of copyrighted works nor provided a service tailored to infringement, and accordingly Cox is not contributorily liable for the infringement of Sony’s copyrights. (No. 24-171, opinion by Justice Thomas; 607 U.S. 583).

title: Supreme Court: Zorn v. Linton
summary: Because the Second Circuit failed to identify a case where an officer using a routine wristlock on a protester after issuing a verbal warning, without more, was held to have violated the Constitution, Sergeant Jacob Zorn was entitled to qualified immunity; the Second Circuit’s contrary conclusion was erroneous. (No. 25-297, opinion by the Court (per curiam); 607 U.S. 568).

title: Supreme Court: Olivier v. City of Brandon
summary: Petitioner Gabriel Olivier’s suit seeking purely prospective relief—an injunction stopping officials from enforcing an ordinance in the future—can proceed, notwithstanding his prior conviction for violating that ordinance; Heck v. Humphrey, 512 U. S. 477 (1994), does not hold otherwise. (No. 24-993, opinion by Justice Kagan; 607 U.S. 552).

title: Supreme Court: Urias-Orellana v. Bondi
summary: The Immigration and Nationality Act requires application of the substantial-evidence standard to the Board of Immigration Appeals’ agency’s determination whether a given set of undisputed facts rises to the level of persecution under 8 U. S. C. §1101(a)(42)(A). (No. 24-777, opinion by Justice Jackson; 607 U.S. 537).

title: Supreme Court: Galette v. New Jersey Transit Corp.
summary: The New Jersey Transit Corporation is not an arm of the State of New Jersey and thus is not entitled to share in New Jersey’s interstate sovereign immunity. (No. 24-1021, opinion by Justice Sotomayor; 607 U.S. 509).

title: Supreme Court: Mirabelli v. Bonta
summary: The application filed by parents and teachers to vacate the Ninth Circuit’s stay of the District Court’s injunction pending appeal is granted as to the parents under the four-factor test in Alabama Assn. of Realtors v. Department of Health and Human Servs., 594 U. S. 758, 763 (2021) (per curiam). (No. 25A810, opinion by the Court (per curiam); 607 U.S. 492).
